newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania police ring square to prevent rally.
newsitem.headline: Albania police ring square to prevent rally.

text.p: Truckloads of police ringed the central square in the Albanian capital on Saturday to prevent opposition parties from staging a rally to denounce the right-wing government and the collapse of pyramid investment schemes.

Skanderberg square was virtually empty as police whisked people away down side streets. About 500 marchers were stopped about one km (600 yards) away from the square and correspondents saw three prominent members of the opposition Socialist Party bundled into a van and driven away.
Albania police ring square to prevent rally =2

The interior ministry had banned the rally, citing security risks after mass rallies against President Sali Berisha in the southern port of Vlore. But a convoy of cars supporting the president's Democratic Party sped unimpeded down city streets with horns blaring.

At least 30,000 demonstrators poured through the streets of Vlore in the fourth consecutive day of protests blaming the president for the failure of the schemes which have left hundreds of thousands of Albanians penniless.
The protests spread to the town of Fier, where about 2,000 anti-government protesters massed to demand refunds of their lost investments. Riot police kept them out of the main square.
Protesters last month set fire to public buildings in several cities, but demonstrators were deterred for a time by 150 arrests and threats of long jail terms on public order charges.
